subproblem.title: Subdivision of [−R, R]ⁿ into Mⁿ convex subcubes of diameter ≤ √n·2R/M covering closedBall(0, R)
subproblem.statement: Let n, M ∈ ℕ with M > 0 and let R ∈ ℝ with R ≥ 0. There is a family (Q_α) of subsets of ℝⁿ indexed by α : Fin n → Fin M (so M^n sets) such that every Q_α is convex, Q_α ⊆ closedBall(0, √n·R), |u − v| ≤ √n·(2R/M) for all u, v ∈ Q_α, and closedBall(0, R) ⊆ ⋃_α Q_α. Notation: ℝ^d = Rn d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) with Euclidean norm |·| and inner product ⟨·,·⟩; Lᵈ = volume on ℝ^d (applied to an arbitrary set it is the Lebesgue outer measure); Hˢ = μHE[s] (Euclidean-normalized Hausdorff outer measure) and μH[s] the unnormalized Hausdorff measure; diam = Metric.ediam (extended diameter in [0,∞]); DF(u) = fderiv ℝ F u with the operator norm ‖·‖; ofReal = ENNReal.ofReal; natural-number subtraction m − 1.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n M : ℕ) (R : ℝ), 0 < M → 0 ≤ R → ∃ Q : (Fin n → Fin M) → Set (Rn n), (∀ α, Convex ℝ (Q α)) ∧ (∀ α, Q α ⊆ Metric.closedBall 0 (Real.sqrt n * R)) ∧ (∀ α, ∀ u ∈ Q α, ∀ v ∈ Q α, dist u v ≤ Real.sqrt n * (2 * R / M)) ∧ Metric.closedBall (0 : Rn n) R ⊆ ⋃ α, Q α
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the supplied proof of c1_critical_slices_null (division of a cube into M^n closed subcubes of side s and diameter √n·s), applied to the cube [−R, R]ⁿ ⊇ closedBall(0, R) with side s := 2R/M; the countable exhaustion of ℝⁿ is by the balls closedBall(0, R), R ∈ ℕ, instead of the unit cubes z + [0, 1]ⁿ.
Write u_i for the i-th coordinate of u ∈ ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), and regard α_i ∈ Fin M as the real number α_i ∈ {0, …, M − 1}. Let s := 2R/M, so s ≥ 0 and s·M = 2R. For α : Fin n → Fin M define
   Q_α := {u ∈ ℝⁿ : −R + s·α_i ≤ u_i ≤ −R + s·(α_i + 1) for every i}.
1. (Convexity.) Let u, v ∈ Q_α and a, b ≥ 0 with a + b = 1. For each i, (au + bv)_i = a u_i + b v_i. Multiplying the bounds for u_i and v_i by a ≥ 0 and b ≥ 0 and adding, with a·L + b·L = L for L = −R + s·α_i and for L = −R + s·(α_i + 1), gives −R + s·α_i ≤ a u_i + b v_i ≤ −R + s·(α_i + 1). Hence au + bv ∈ Q_α.
2. (Q_α ⊆ closedBall(0, √n·R).) Let u ∈ Q_α and fix i. Since α_i ≥ 0 and s ≥ 0, u_i ≥ −R + s·α_i ≥ −R. Since α_i + 1 ≤ M, u_i ≤ −R + s·(α_i + 1) ≤ −R + s·M = R. Hence |u_i| ≤ R and u_i² ≤ R². Therefore |u| = (Σ_i u_i²)^{1/2} ≤ (Σ_{i ∈ Fin n} R²)^{1/2} = (n·R²)^{1/2} = √n·R (EuclideanSpace.norm_eq, Real.sqrt_le_sqrt, Real.sqrt_mul, Real.sqrt_sq with R ≥ 0).
3. (Diameter.) Let u, v ∈ Q_α. For each i, u_i and v_i both lie in the interval [−R + s·α_i, −R + s·(α_i + 1)] of length s, so |u_i − v_i| ≤ s. Hence |u − v| = (Σ_i (u_i − v_i)²)^{1/2} ≤ (n·s²)^{1/2} = √n·s = √n·(2R/M) (EuclideanSpace.dist_eq, s ≥ 0).
4. (Covering.) Let u ∈ closedBall(0, R), i.e. |u| ≤ R. Then |u_i| ≤ |u| ≤ R for every i (PiLp.norm_apply_le).
   • If R = 0, then u_i = 0 for all i and s = 0. Take α ≡ 0 (possible since M > 0): the defining inequalities read 0 ≤ u_i ≤ 0, which hold, so u ∈ Q_α.
   • If R > 0, then s > 0. For each i put t_i := (u_i + R)/s. Since 0 ≤ u_i + R ≤ 2R = s·M, we get 0 ≤ t_i ≤ M. Put α_i := min(⌊t_i⌋, M − 1) ∈ {0, …, M − 1} (⌊·⌋ the natural-number floor, Nat.floor). Then α_i ≤ ⌊t_i⌋ ≤ t_i (Nat.floor_le, t_i ≥ 0). Also t_i ≤ α_i + 1: if ⌊t_i⌋ ≤ M − 1 then α_i = ⌊t_i⌋ and t_i < ⌊t_i⌋ + 1 (Nat.lt_floor_add_one); otherwise α_i = M − 1 and t_i ≤ M = (M − 1) + 1 (M ≥ 1). Since u_i = −R + s·t_i and s > 0, it follows that −R + s·α_i ≤ u_i ≤ −R + s·(α_i + 1) for every i, i.e. u ∈ Q_α.
   In both cases u ∈ ⋃_α Q_α. ∎
proof_key_steps: Define Q_α := {u : −R + sα_i ≤ u_i ≤ −R + s(α_i+1) ∀ i} with s = 2R/M (subcubes of [−R,R]ⁿ).
Each Q_α is an intersection of coordinate slabs, hence convex.
Coordinates of points of Q_α lie in [−R, R], so |u| ≤ √n·R; two points of Q_α differ by ≤ s in each coordinate, so |u − v| ≤ √n·s.
For |u| ≤ R choose α_i = min(⌊(u_i + R)/s⌋, M − 1) (any α if R = 0), giving u ∈ Q_α.

audit.reason: The exact type matches all four asserted family properties and both hypotheses. Explicit coordinate intervals prove convexity, ball containment and the Euclidean distance bound. The clipped-floor construction covers boundary points correctly, with R=0 handled separately and n=0 valid. This is a complete independent obligation.

subproblem.title: Fine covers with small weighted image volume give Hᵏ-null slices for Lᵐ-a.e. y (Fatou covering criterion)
subproblem.statement: Let n, m, k ∈ ℕ with k > 0, let S ⊆ ℝⁿ be an arbitrary set and G : ℝⁿ → ℝᵐ an arbitrary map. Suppose that for every ε ∈ (0, ∞] there are a countable index type ι and sets T_i ⊆ ℝⁿ (i ∈ ι) such that S ⊆ ⋃_i T_i, diam T_i ≤ ε for every i, and Σ_i (diam T_i)^k · Lᵐ(G(T_i ∩ S)) ≤ ε (a sum in [0, ∞]; Lᵐ is applied as an outer measure to the possibly non-measurable sets G(T_i ∩ S)). Then Hᵏ(S ∩ G⁻¹{y}) = 0 for Lᵐ-a.e. y ∈ ℝᵐ. Notation: ℝ^d = Rn d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) with Euclidean norm |·| and inner product ⟨·,·⟩; Lᵈ = volume on ℝ^d (applied to an arbitrary set it is the Lebesgue outer measure); Hˢ = μHE[s] (Euclidean-normalized Hausdorff outer measure) and μH[s] the unnormalized Hausdorff measure; diam = Metric.ediam (extended diameter in [0,∞]); DF(u) = fderiv ℝ F u with the operator norm ‖·‖; ofReal = ENNReal.ofReal; natural-number subtraction m − 1.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n m k : ℕ) (S : Set (Rn n)) (G : Rn n → Rn m), 0 < k → (∀ ε : ℝ≥0∞, 0 < ε → ∃ (ι : Type) (_ : Countable ι) (T : ι → Set (Rn n)), S ⊆ ⋃ i, T i ∧ (∀ i, Metric.ediam (T i) ≤ ε) ∧ ∑' i, Metric.ediam (T i) ^ k * volume (G '' (T i ∩ S)) ≤ ε) → ∀ᵐ y ∂(volume : Measure (Rn m)), μHE[k] (S ∩ G ⁻¹' {y}) = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 6–8 of the supplied proof of c1_critical_slices_null (Simon Ch. 2, p. 66, the consequence of (6.3) stated before 6.4, book/chapter-02.txt lines 1476–1478; Simon gives no proof), i.e. the Borel majorants, the covering estimate and Fatou's lemma, abstracted from the subcube covers to arbitrary countable covers. The only change is that the Borel majorant uses a measurable hull of G(T_i ∩ S) instead of the compactness of G(Q ∩ C); hence no topological or measurability hypothesis on S or G is needed.
1. (Covers at scales ε_j.) For j ∈ ℕ put ε_j := (j+1)⁻¹ ∈ (0, ∞). Then ε_j → 0 as j → ∞ (ENNReal.tendsto_inv_nat_nhds_zero composed with j ↦ j + 1). Apply the hypothesis with ε = ε_j and choose a countable index type ι_j and sets T_{j,i} (i ∈ ι_j) with (a) S ⊆ ⋃_i T_{j,i}, (b) diam T_{j,i} ≤ ε_j for all i, (c) Σ_i (diam T_{j,i})^k · Lᵐ(G(T_{j,i} ∩ S)) ≤ ε_j.
2. (Measurable hulls.) For all j, i let A_{j,i} := toMeasurable(Lᵐ, G(T_{j,i} ∩ S)). It is a measurable set, G(T_{j,i} ∩ S) ⊆ A_{j,i}, and Lᵐ(A_{j,i}) = Lᵐ(G(T_{j,i} ∩ S)) (Mathlib measurableSet_toMeasurable, subset_toMeasurable, measure_toMeasurable).
3. (Majorants.) Define g_j : ℝᵐ → [0, ∞] by g_j(y) := Σ_{i ∈ ι_j} (diam T_{j,i})^k · 1_{A_{j,i}}(y). Each summand is a constant times the indicator of a measurable set, hence measurable, and a countable sum of measurable [0, ∞]-valued functions is measurable (Measurable.tsum, formerly Measurable.ennreal_tsum); so g_j is measurable. By the monotone convergence theorem for countable sums (lintegral_tsum), ∫⁻ c·1_A = c·Lᵐ(A) for measurable A (lintegral_const_mul, lintegral_indicator_one), and step 2,
   ∫ g_j dLᵐ = Σ_i (diam T_{j,i})^k · Lᵐ(A_{j,i}) = Σ_i (diam T_{j,i})^k · Lᵐ(G(T_{j,i} ∩ S)) ≤ ε_j by 1(c).
4. (Fatou.) Let h(y) := liminf_{j→∞} g_j(y); h is measurable as a liminf of a sequence of measurable functions (Measurable.liminf). By Fatou's lemma (lintegral_liminf_le) and step 3, ∫ h dLᵐ ≤ liminf_j ∫ g_j dLᵐ ≤ liminf_j ε_j = 0. Hence ∫ h dLᵐ = 0 and, h being measurable, h(y) = 0 for Lᵐ-a.e. y (lintegral_eq_zero_iff).
5. (Covering estimate.) Fix y with h(y) = 0. For all j, i put t_{j,i} := T_{j,i} ∩ (S ∩ G⁻¹{y}). Then diam t_{j,i} ≤ diam T_{j,i} ≤ ε_j for all j, i, and S ∩ G⁻¹{y} ⊆ ⋃_i t_{j,i} for every j, since every u ∈ S lies in some T_{j,i} by 1(a). The covering bound for the Hausdorff measure with countable covers whose diameters are bounded by r_j → 0 (Mathlib Measure.hausdorffMeasure_le_liminf_tsum with d = k, r_j = ε_j and the filter atTop) gives
   μH[k](S ∩ G⁻¹{y}) ≤ liminf_j Σ_i (diam t_{j,i})^k
   (in Mathlib the power is the real power (diam)^(k:ℝ), which equals the natural power, ENNReal.rpow_natCast).
6. (Comparison with g_j.) For all j, i: (diam t_{j,i})^k ≤ (diam T_{j,i})^k · 1_{A_{j,i}}(y). Indeed, if t_{j,i} = ∅ then diam t_{j,i} = 0 and 0^k = 0 because k > 0. If t_{j,i} contains a point u, then u ∈ T_{j,i} ∩ S and G(u) = y, so y ∈ G(T_{j,i} ∩ S) ⊆ A_{j,i}; the indicator equals 1 and (diam t_{j,i})^k ≤ (diam T_{j,i})^k by monotonicity of the diameter and of x ↦ x^k on [0, ∞]. Summing over i (ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum) gives Σ_i (diam t_{j,i})^k ≤ g_j(y) for every j, and monotonicity of liminf (liminf_le_liminf) with step 5 gives μH[k](S ∩ G⁻¹{y}) ≤ liminf_j g_j(y) = h(y) = 0.
7. (Conclusion.) By definition μHE[k] = c_k · μH[k] with the constant c_k := addHaarScalarFactor(volume on ℝᵏ, μH[k]) (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def), so μHE[k](S ∩ G⁻¹{y}) = c_k · 0 = 0. This holds for every y with h(y) = 0, hence for Lᵐ-a.e. y ∈ ℝᵐ. ∎
proof_key_steps: Choose countable covers (T_{j,i})_i of S at scales ε_j = (j+1)⁻¹ → 0 with Σ_i (diam T_{j,i})^k Lᵐ(G(T_{j,i}∩S)) ≤ ε_j.
Measurable hulls A_{j,i} ⊇ G(T_{j,i}∩S) of equal measure give measurable majorants g_j = Σ_i (diam T_{j,i})^k 1_{A_{j,i}} with ∫ g_j ≤ ε_j.
Fatou's lemma gives ∫ liminf_j g_j = 0, so liminf_j g_j(y) = 0 for Lᵐ-a.e. y.
For such y the covers T_{j,i} ∩ S ∩ G⁻¹{y} and hausdorffMeasure_le_liminf_tsum give μH[k](S∩G⁻¹{y}) ≤ liminf_j g_j(y) = 0 (empty pieces contribute 0^k = 0 as k > 0).
μHE[k] = c_k·μH[k], so Hᵏ(S∩G⁻¹{y}) = 0 for Lᵐ-a.e. y.

audit.reason: The exact type matches the prose, including arbitrary S and G and countable covers. Equal-measure measurable hulls justify the measurable majorants without extra hypotheses. Countable integration and Fatou give zero liminf almost everywhere; shrinking fiber covers, k>0 for empty pieces, and Hausdorff normalization prove the exact conclusion. The proof is complete and non-circular.

subproblem.title: Volume of a slab intersected with a ball: Lᵐ ≤ 2r(2R)^{m−1}
subproblem.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, let ν, c ∈ ℝᵐ with |ν| = 1, and let r, R ∈ ℝ. Then Lᵐ({w ∈ ℝᵐ : |⟨w − c, ν⟩| ≤ r and |w − c| ≤ R}) ≤ ofReal(2r·(2R)^{m−1}), i.e. the volume of the slab of half-width r normal to ν, intersected with the closed ball of radius R about c, is at most max(0, 2r(2R)^{m−1}). Notation: ℝ^d = Rn d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) with Euclidean norm |·| and inner product ⟨·,·⟩; Lᵈ = volume on ℝ^d (applied to an arbitrary set it is the Lebesgue outer measure); Hˢ = μHE[s] (Euclidean-normalized Hausdorff outer measure) and μH[s] the unnormalized Hausdorff measure; diam = Metric.ediam (extended diameter in [0,∞]); DF(u) = fderiv ℝ F u with the operator norm ‖·‖; ofReal = ENNReal.ofReal; natural-number subtraction m − 1.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (ν c : Rn m) (r R : ℝ), ‖ν‖ = 1 → volume {w : Rn m | |inner ℝ (w - c) ν| ≤ r ∧ ‖w - c‖ ≤ R} ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (2 * r * (2 * R) ^ (m - 1))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the last two sentences of step 5 of the supplied proof of c1_critical_slices_null ("A linear isometry of ℝᵐ taking ν to the first basis vector preserves Lᵐ and maps this set of w into the box [−r, r] × [−R, R]^{m−1}. Therefore Lᵐ(...) ≤ 2r·(2R)^{m−1}"), with the translation by c and the degenerate cases made explicit.
Let W := {w ∈ ℝᵐ : |⟨w − c, ν⟩| ≤ r and |w − c| ≤ R}.
1. (Degenerate radii.) If r < 0 then W = ∅, because |⟨w − c, ν⟩| ≥ 0 > r. If R < 0 then W = ∅, because |w − c| ≥ 0 > R. In both cases Lᵐ(W) = 0 ≤ ofReal(2r(2R)^{m−1}). From now on r ≥ 0 and R ≥ 0.
2. (m ≥ 1.) If m = 0 then ℝ⁰ = {0}, so ν = 0 and |ν| = 0 ≠ 1, a contradiction. Hence m = m' + 1 with m' = m − 1.
3. (Rotation taking ν to e₀.) Let e₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 be the first standard basis vector, so |e₀| = 1 = |ν|. Let ρ be the orthogonal reflection of ℝᵐ in the subspace (ℝ·(ν − e₀))^⊥ (Mathlib Submodule.reflection). It is a linear isometry equivalence of ℝᵐ, and ρ(ν) = e₀ because |ν| = |e₀| (Submodule.reflection_sub; if ν = e₀ the subspace is all of ℝᵐ and ρ is the identity).
4. (W lies in a box after translation and rotation.) Put Φ(w) := ρ(w − c) and write x = Φ(w) with coordinates x_0, …, x_{m'}. Let a := (−r, −R, …, −R) and b := (r, R, …, R) ∈ ℝ^{Fin m} (first coordinate ±r, the others ±R). For w ∈ W:
   • x_0 = ⟨x, e₀⟩ (EuclideanSpace.inner_single_right) = ⟨ρ(w − c), ρ(ν)⟩ = ⟨w − c, ν⟩ (ρ preserves inner products, LinearIsometryEquiv.inner_map_map), so −r ≤ x_0 ≤ r;
   • for every coordinate i, |x_i| ≤ |x| (PiLp.norm_apply_le) = |w − c| (ρ is an isometry) ≤ R, so −R ≤ x_i ≤ R; this is used for i ≠ 0.
   Hence the coordinate vector of Φ(w) lies in the box Icc a b, i.e. W ⊆ (ofLp ∘ ρ ∘ (· − c))⁻¹(Icc a b), where ofLp : ℝᵐ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m) → (Fin m → ℝ) is the coordinate map.
5. (Measure preservation.) The translation w ↦ w − c preserves Lebesgue measure (measurePreserving_sub_right), ρ preserves Lebesgue measure because it is a linear isometry equivalence of a finite-dimensional inner product space (LinearIsometryEquiv.measurePreserving), and ofLp carries volume on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m) to the product Lebesgue measure on Fin m → ℝ (PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp). So the composite ofLp ∘ ρ ∘ (· − c) is measure preserving, and since the box Icc a b is measurable, Lᵐ((ofLp ∘ ρ ∘ (· − c))⁻¹(Icc a b)) = L^{Fin m}(Icc a b) (MeasurePreserving.measure_preimage).
6. (Box volume.) By Real.volume_Icc_pi, L^{Fin m}(Icc a b) = Π_{i ∈ Fin m} ofReal(b_i − a_i) = ofReal(2r) · Π_{i ∈ Fin m'} ofReal(2R) (Fin.prod_univ_succ) = ofReal(2r) · ofReal(2R)^{m'} = ofReal(2r·(2R)^{m'}) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul and ENNReal.ofReal_pow, using r, R ≥ 0), and m' = m − 1.
7. By monotonicity of Lᵐ and steps 4–6, Lᵐ(W) ≤ ofReal(2r·(2R)^{m−1}). ∎
proof_key_steps: If r < 0 or R < 0 the set is empty; otherwise |ν| = 1 forces m = m' + 1 ≥ 1.
The reflection ρ in (ℝ(ν − e₀))^⊥ is a linear isometry equivalence with ρ(ν) = e₀.
w ↦ ρ(w − c) maps the set into the box [−r,r] × [−R,R]^{m'}, since ⟨ρ(w−c), e₀⟩ = ⟨w−c, ν⟩ and |x_i| ≤ |x| = |w − c|.
Translation, ρ and the coordinate map ofLp preserve Lebesgue measure, and the box has volume 2r·(2R)^{m−1}.

audit.reason: The type matches the statement with unrestricted real radii. Negative radii give an empty set, and the unit-vector hypothesis excludes m=0. Reflection, translation and the coordinate map preserve the intended volume; containment in the coordinate box gives the stated bound. Zero radii and ν=e₀ are covered without additional assumptions.

subproblem.title: Image of a convex set under a map whose derivative is close to a non-surjective linear map has small volume
subproblem.statement: Let n, m ∈ ℕ, G : ℝⁿ → ℝᵐ, S ⊆ ℝⁿ convex, u₀ ∈ S, P : ℝⁿ → ℝᵐ a continuous linear map that is not surjective, and d, ε, Λ ∈ ℝ. Suppose that G is differentiable at every point of S, that ‖DG(v) − P‖ ≤ ε for every v ∈ S (operator norm), that |v − u₀| ≤ d for every v ∈ S, and that ‖P‖ ≤ Λ. Then Lᵐ(G(S)) ≤ ofReal(2(εd)·(2(Λ + ε)d)^{m−1}). Notation: ℝ^d = Rn d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) with Euclidean norm |·| and inner product ⟨·,·⟩; Lᵈ = volume on ℝ^d (applied to an arbitrary set it is the Lebesgue outer measure); Hˢ = μHE[s] (Euclidean-normalized Hausdorff outer measure) and μH[s] the unnormalized Hausdorff measure; diam = Metric.ediam (extended diameter in [0,∞]); DF(u) = fderiv ℝ F u with the operator norm ‖·‖; ofReal = ENNReal.ofReal; natural-number subtraction m − 1.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n m : ℕ) (G : Rn n → Rn m) (S : Set (Rn n)) (P : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn m) (u₀ : Rn n) (d ε Λ : ℝ), Convex ℝ S → u₀ ∈ S → (∀ v ∈ S, DifferentiableAt ℝ G v) → (∀ v ∈ S, ‖fderiv ℝ G v - P‖ ≤ ε) → (∀ v ∈ S, ‖v - u₀‖ ≤ d) → ¬ Function.Surjective P → ‖P‖ ≤ Λ → volume (G '' S) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (2 * (ε * d) * (2 * ((Λ + ε) * d)) ^ (m - 1))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the supplied proof of c1_critical_slices_null ("the image of a critical subcube lies in a thin slab"), with the subcube Q replaced by an arbitrary convex set S of radius d about u₀, the tolerance 1/j by ε, and the bound ‖DG‖ ≤ Λ on the cube by the hypothesis ‖P‖ ≤ Λ. Uses the sibling slab_volume (critSlices_slab_volume_le).
1. (Signs.) Since u₀ ∈ S, ε ≥ ‖DG(u₀) − P‖ ≥ 0 and d ≥ |u₀ − u₀| = 0.
2. (A unit normal to the range of P.) Let V := range P, a linear subspace of ℝᵐ. V ≠ ℝᵐ because P is not surjective. In the finite-dimensional space ℝᵐ, V^⊥ = {0} holds iff V = ℝᵐ (Submodule.orthogonal_eq_bot_iff; finite-dimensional subspaces are complete and so have orthogonal projections), so there is ν₀ ∈ V^⊥ with ν₀ ≠ 0 (Submodule.exists_mem_ne_zero_of_ne_bot). Put ν := |ν₀|⁻¹ ν₀. Then |ν| = 1 and ⟨P x, ν⟩ = |ν₀|⁻¹ ⟨P x, ν₀⟩ = 0 for every x ∈ ℝⁿ, because P x ∈ V and ν₀ ∈ V^⊥ (Submodule.mem_orthogonal).
3. (Mean value inequality.) Let u ∈ S. G is differentiable at every point of the convex set S and ‖DG(v) − P‖ ≤ ε for v ∈ S, so the mean value inequality for G − P on S (Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_fderiv_le') gives, for e := G(u) − G(u₀) − P(u − u₀), |e| ≤ ε|u − u₀| ≤ εd, using ε ≥ 0 and |u − u₀| ≤ d.
4. (The image lies in a slab.) Let w := G(u) − G(u₀) = P(u − u₀) + e. Then ⟨w, ν⟩ = ⟨P(u − u₀), ν⟩ + ⟨e, ν⟩ = ⟨e, ν⟩ by step 2, so by Cauchy–Schwarz |⟨w, ν⟩| ≤ |e||ν| = |e| ≤ εd. Moreover |w| ≤ |P(u − u₀)| + |e| ≤ ‖P‖ |u − u₀| + εd ≤ Λd + εd = (Λ + ε)d, using ‖P‖ ≤ Λ, |u − u₀| ≤ d, |u − u₀| ≥ 0 and Λ ≥ ‖P‖ ≥ 0.
5. (Conclusion.) By step 4, G(S) ⊆ W := {w' ∈ ℝᵐ : |⟨w' − G(u₀), ν⟩| ≤ εd and |w' − G(u₀)| ≤ (Λ + ε)d}. The sibling slab_volume (critSlices_slab_volume_le applied with this m, ν, c := G(u₀), r := εd, R := (Λ + ε)d, and |ν| = 1) gives Lᵐ(W) ≤ ofReal(2(εd)·(2((Λ + ε)d))^{m−1}). By monotonicity of Lᵐ (measure_mono), Lᵐ(G(S)) ≤ Lᵐ(W) ≤ ofReal(2(εd)·(2(Λ + ε)d)^{m−1}). ∎
proof_key_steps: u₀ ∈ S gives ε ≥ 0 and d ≥ 0.
P not surjective gives a unit vector ν ⊥ range P (Submodule.orthogonal_eq_bot_iff).
Mean value inequality for G − P on convex S: |G(u) − G(u₀) − P(u − u₀)| ≤ εd.
Hence G(S) lies in {w : |⟨w − G(u₀), ν⟩| ≤ εd, |w − G(u₀)| ≤ (Λ+ε)d}.
Apply slab_volume (critSlices_slab_volume_le) with r = εd, R = (Λ+ε)d.

Non-surjectivity gives a unit normal; the convex-set mean-value inequality gives the remainder estimate and both slab constraints. Applying the declared slab_volume dependency proves the conclusion without parent reliance.
